problem_type: Static MCP reference gate recognizes only one object-property spelling and misses positional tool calls.
symptom: The existing check:mcp-tool-refs exited 0 while tests/ux contained 9 callTool('nomi_generate', ...) calls to a retired MCP tool.
direct_cause: The gate matched only name: 'nomi_x' properties in tests/ux and never inspected positional callTool arguments or executable documentation examples.
class_root: Tool-reference validation had no shared reference extractor for the equivalent MCP call shapes, so a retired name could remain callable in an unrun walkthrough without failing Contracts.
affected_population: Contributors changing the MCP catalog or migrating tests
CI reviewers relying on unrun UX walkthroughs as evidence
Executable examples under tests/ and docs/ that call MCP tools by position or template literal
internal_only_reason: The invariant is entirely internal: MCP_TOOL_RESOLVER is the repository's catalog truth source and the failure is a repository static-gate gap.
invariants: Every statically recognizable MCP tool reference in tests/ and executable docs examples resolves in MCP_TOOL_RESOLVER.
Intentional unknown-tool probes remain explicit with unknown-tool-probe and are not confused with stale calls.
Host fixture tool names are checked against the agent catalog only when the call site visibly has type: 'tool'.
NUL-containing source files are read and scanned instead of being silently skipped.
generality_proof: All supported spellings converge through scanSource: positional callTool-like calls, name properties in tools/call payloads, and template literals use the same catalog set. The scan covers every tests subtree except the independently scoped synthetic agent-runtime fixtures and all executable documentation fences, so another caller cannot reintroduce this exact blind spot by changing syntax or location.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Extract equivalent MCP tool-reference shapes and associate each with the correct MCP or host catalog.
Run the shared extractor over tests and executable docs in the Contracts gate.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: These names feed a fake Pi/HTTP tool pipeline and do not call the MCP service; the scanner excludes this independently scoped fixture directory.
The gate derives its declared set from MCP_TOOL_RESOLVER.list() and does not maintain a second hand-written name list.

recurrence.reason: Any future catalog retirement can be hidden by a different call syntax or by an executable example outside the former tests/ux-only scan.
same_class_scan: rg -n "nomi_generate" tests/ux --glob '*.mjs' found 9 calls across four unreferenced walkthrough files
rg -n "draft-journey|mcp-draft-loop|spend-elicit-app-open|workbench-token-root-scope" package.json .github scripts found no runner references

prevention.invariant: All supported executable MCP reference shapes resolve against the catalog truth source, while host fixtures use their own visible catalog boundary.
prevention.failure_mode: A stale or retired tool name makes check:mcp-tool-refs exit 1 with file and line; only an explicitly marked unknown-tool-probe is exempt.
prevention.strategy: Centralize extraction in scanSource, run it in Contracts over tests and executable docs, and prove the class boundary with node:test fixtures including NUL input.

legacy_paths.rationale: All four walkthroughs were unreferenced by package/workflow runners and depended on the retired nomi_generate path. P1 removes the obsolete tests instead of replacing a paid legacy call with an invented non-equivalent operation sequence.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime or dependency controls this static reference invariant.

migration: No user data migration. The gate command now runs its node-test before the catalog scan; obsolete unrun walkthrough files are deleted in the same change.
residual_risks: Dynamic string concatenation or interpolated template names cannot be resolved statically and remain outside this gate; such callers must use a literal or add a dedicated runtime contract.
The synthetic tests/agent-runtime fixture directory remains intentionally outside this MCP catalog gate and is covered by its own agent-runtime tests.
